detailed_rationale:
Whirlpool of India Ltd manufactures and markets major home appliances (refrigerators, washing machines, air conditioners) under the Whirlpool brand, majority-owned by US parent Whirlpool Corp. FY26 sales were essentially flat at Rs 8,034cr (vs Rs 7,919cr in FY25), but net profit fell 19% to Rs 295cr from Rs 363cr - margin erosion despite steady volumes. Quarterly results have been choppy: profit swung from Rs 27cr (Dec 2025) to Rs 146cr (Jun 2026), with the seasonally stronger summer-cooling quarter driving the bulk of annual profit, as is typical for the category.

The more important development is ownership: promoter (Whirlpool Corp) holding has fallen from 75% in Mar 2023 to 51% and now to 39.76% in Mar 2026, with domestic institutions absorbing the bulk of the sell-down (DII stake now 35.85%). A multi-year, multi-tranche reduction in strategic ownership by the US parent is a genuine signal about the parent's long-term commitment to the India business, on top of an already-stalling growth and margin trajectory (5-year sales CAGR ~6.4%, 5-year profit CAGR negative).

The balance sheet itself is clean - minimal debt, comfortable interest coverage - but that financial strength is not translating into growth or margin expansion in a category (appliances) where Indian majors (Voltas, Havells) and Korean/Japanese competitors (LG, Samsung, Daikin, Haier) are all fighting hard for share. At a P/E of ~33x for a company with declining profit and a fading parent commitment, we don't see the risk/reward as favourable.
recommendation_rationale: Declining profit, stalling growth, and a multi-year promoter (parent) stake reduction together outweigh the clean, debt-free balance sheet. The valuation (33x earnings) is not undemanding enough to compensate for a business that is losing share and momentum, so this stays a Sell with no rescue.
summary: Whirlpool India's appliance business has seen sales stagnate and profit decline over the past year, in a competitive market where Indian and other multinational appliance makers are all fighting for share. The US parent has also been steadily reducing its ownership stake over the past three years, from 75% to under 40%, which is worth watching as a signal of long-term commitment. The balance sheet is clean, but growth and profitability trends do not currently support the stock's valuation.
positive_para: Debt-free balance sheet with strong interest coverage; an established, recognised appliance brand with long India operating history; India's structural appliance-penetration growth (rising incomes, urbanisation, warming climate boosting AC/refrigeration demand) provides a genuine long-term category tailwind even if this specific company is not currently capturing it well.
negative_para: Profit fell 19% in FY26 despite flat revenue - clear margin compression; five-year sales CAGR of only ~6% and five-year profit CAGR negative show a business that has stopped compounding; and the promoter's stake reduction from 75% to under 40% over three years is a real governance/commitment signal that should not be waved away as routine.
reverse_dcf_judgment: A P/E near 33x implies double-digit sustained earnings growth; Whirlpool India has instead delivered a negative 5-year profit CAGR and a 19% profit decline in the most recent year. The multiple is not supported by the trend, and the parent's declining strategic commitment adds execution-risk on top of that gap.
